thread:
marta: Heads-up — hitting a weird SSE parsing edge in the Node sample app when the client aborts mid-stream. final delimiter line `

` seems to be lost and parser glues last partial JSON to the first chunk on reconnect.
kevin: which Node SDK version? have a minimal repro?
marta: node-sdk@1.3.4. Repro: start streaming a long completion (~8 chunks), call `controller.abort()` after chunk 6, then immediately re-open a new streaming request. Often the parser emits `SyntaxError: Unexpected token` on the first message after reconnect.
jun: can you paste the chunk boundaries/logs? wondering if the server omitted the blank line or if client trimmed it.
marta: paste of raw frames below (sanitized):
```
data: {"id":1,"delta":"foo"}


data: {"id":2,"delta":"bar"}


data: {"id":3,"delta":"baz"}


<client abort here>
[data after reconnect comes back as]
data: {"id":4,"delta":"qux"}

```
kevin: aha. looks like between chunk 3 and 4 we expected `

` but client-side buffer ends with `...baz"}

` sometimes the abort drops the trailing newline leaving `...baz"}
` and next `data:` attaches -> `...baz"}
data:` -> parse fails if we treat whole thing as JSON.
lucy: is the Node parser using a split-on-double-newline implementation? we might be trimming trailing newlines in the abort path.
marta: yes it's a simple stateful line buffer in `event-stream/parser.js` in sample app. Behavior differs vs python sample which tolerates lone `
`.
kevin: quick mitigation: treat any `
data:` boundary as valid if previous buffer ends with `}` not `}

`. i can open a tiny PR to make the parser resilient to single-newline separators and to accept `
data:` as start.
jun: also worth checking `last-event-id` handling. If we resume and send a `Last-Event-ID` header, we must not re-emit incomplete JSON. Might need to stash the partial chunk to `resumeBuffers` keyed by client id.
marta: for immediate fix, i hacked the sample app to flush on `abort` and it reduced the frequency. But we should fix the SDK parser to be tolerant (both Node and Browser).
ci-bot: deploy pipeline (dev-sample) started for branches: kevin/fix-sse-boundary  — build #842 queued.
kevin: opening PR now: minimal change in parser to accept `
` or `

` as delimiter and to trim leading `data:` when it's glued. also added test cases for `abort` + reconnect and for `
`-only separators.
lucy: please add a spec test that simulates `controller.abort()` mid-frame and immediate reconnect. that's what flaked in our CI.
marta: noted. added a short checklist in the PR body: reproduction steps, flaky logs, backoff recommendation (add 50–200ms jitter before reconnect), and compatibility note with python client.
jun: quick question: do we want to change server behavior instead (always send `

` after each chunk)? that would be safer but breaking for other consumers.\e marta: prefer client-side fix first. server change is more intrusive and could mask underlying transport races.
kevin: PR: https://git.redwood/example/kr/sse-parser-fix (WIP). If reviewers OK, will cut a patch release for node-sdk@1.3.5 and cherry-pick to browser-sdks.
lucy: adding to release notes: "Fix: resilient SSE parser for single-newline chunk boundaries and client abort/reconnect". also add troubleshooting doc: when you see `Unexpected token` after reconnect, restart with `SDK_DEBUG=events` and include raw frames.
marta: thanks — running extended flakiness test now (100 abort/reconnect cycles). will report results in this thread. (reacted :eyes:)
kevin: thanks all — once CI green i'll ship the patch to the sample app and cut the patch release.
marta: final update: after the parser change + 1000 cycles we saw 0 failures locally. putting note in sample app README. last run: `2249001580`
